instructions: Boil about 2 1/2 cups of water in a kettle or small pot. Chop the onion and bell pepper fine. Chop the tomatoes.
Heat the olive oil in a deep pot over medium heat. Add the onion and pepper and cook for 4 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes, until they start to break down.
Add the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until it darkens.
Add the bulgur and stir for 2 minutes.
Turn the heat to high and pour in 2 1/4 cups of the hot water. Add the salt and the black pepper, stir a couple of times and bring to a boil.
Cover, turn the heat to medium-low and cook for 10 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Take the pot off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes.
Uncover and stir with a fork. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Cup of Yum's bulgur pilaf with tomatoes (5 from 6 ratings, under 20) leads. Chocolates and Chai and Cinnamon Snail agree on the order: onion and pepper first, then tomato and paste, then toast the bulgur, then hot water and a covered simmer and rest. Cup of Yum uses 1 1/2 cups water per 200 g bulgur; this uses a slightly higher ratio for 1 1/2 cups. Tomato paste is used because it is easier to find than red pepper paste, and water replaces stock and butter to keep it vegan.
